name: Saint Agnes
history: A Roman girl of about twelve or thirteen who refused marriage because she had consecrated herself to Christ, and was put to death for her faith, probably under Diocletian. Saints Ambrose, Jerome and Augustine all praised her courage. Her name, close to the Latin agnus, lamb, is said in the Roman Canon, and her basilica on the Via Nomentana stands over her tomb.
life: Little is known for certain about Agnes beyond her youth, her virginity and her martyrdom, but her memory was cherished from the start. Constantina, daughter of Constantine, built a basilica near her tomb, and Pope Damasus set up an inscription in her honour. The story that grew up around her tells of a beautiful girl sought in marriage by young men of Rome, who answered that she was already promised to a Spouse no man could equal. Denounced as a Christian, she was threatened, dragged to a place of shame where tradition says her hair grew to cover her, and finally killed by the sword. Saint Ambrose marvelled that there was hardly room in so small a body for a wound. Each year on her feast two lambs are blessed at her basilica, and their wool is woven into the pallia the Pope gives to new archbishops.
prayerTo: Saint Agnes, child of courage, you gave yourself wholly to Christ and would not take yourself back. Pray for children and young people, for all who are pressed to betray their conscience, and for me, that I may love purity and the truth more than the approval of others. Lamb of God, keep me faithful. Amen.
penance: Pray today for young people under pressure, and give something to a charity that protects children. Offer one small act of self-denial for purity of heart.
meditation: A child was braver than the court that condemned her. What would you hold to, if holding to it cost you everything?
prayer: Almighty, eternal God, You Who choose the weak things of the world to confound the strong, mercifully grant that we who are celebrating the feast of blessed Agnes, Your Virgin and Martyr, may reap the benefit of her patronal intercession with You. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
